docs.title: Horcrux Hardware
docs.text:
This website is a step-by-step guide that teaches complete beginners how to build a Horcrux device entirely from scratch.

This is about the hardware and how you can build it yourself. For more information about the software that runs the device, go to horcrux-core.

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text:
• The philosophy behind Horcrux — why it exists and what problem it solves.
  • How to build a Horcrux device — from the electronic components to the final assembly.
  • How to use it — storing and recovering your secrets in practice.

docs.title: What is a Horcrux?
docs.text:
A Horcrux is a physical device that lets you safely store your most sensitive secrets.

Under the hood, it relies on the Shamir's Secret Sharing algorithm that works the following way:

  1. Your secret is split into multiple pieces (called shares).
  2. Each share is useless on its own — you cannot recover the secret from a single share.
  3. To reconstruct the secret, you need to bring together at least a threshold number of shares.

This means you can distribute your shares across different locations or people, and even if some shares are lost or stolen, your secret remains safe as long as the threshold isn't reached.

docs.title: Why Horcrux?
docs.text:
Horcrux aims to implement Shamir's Secret Sharing in a way that is:

  • Timeless — built with durable, long-lasting hardware.
  • Private — horcrux is not connected to the internet.
  • Secure — designed to protect your data against theft and loss.
  • Open source — anyone can build its own horcrux device for almost nothing.

The core idea is to make this powerful technology available to everyone, giving you full ownership and control over your most sensitive information. All that, without relying on any third party or cloud service that could have a leak or close overnight.

docs.title: What secrets should I store in a Horcrux?
docs.text:
You can store pretty much anything you want to keep secret. However, I'd recommend being selective about what you put inside. A Horcrux is best reserved for your most important secrets — the ones you truly couldn't afford to lose.

Good candidates include, the master password that unlocks your password manager, the recovery phrase or keys that protect your cryptocurrency, or even a private keepsake you don't want to lose.

docs.title: How to build a Horcrux
docs.text:
Building your own Horcrux is a step-by-step journey. The steps below will walk you through each part of the process, from the hardware to how you handle your shares once they exist.

  • Learn more about the brain of the Horcrux device.
  • Learn more about the best ways to create your shares.
  • Learn more about the best ways to distribute your shares.
  • Learn more about how to explain horcrux to people that know nothing about computer science.

docs.title: 1. Setup the hardware
docs.text:
The microcontroller is the brain of your Horcrux device. It runs horcrux-core, the firmware that powers it.

The following boards are currently supported: - ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 - ESP32-DevKit-V1 - Support for more boards is on the way — check back soon...

Note: These boards have been tested and are known to work with horcrux-core. There are probably more that work, but since they haven't been tested, they won't appear on the list.

Note: For now, Horcrux requires boards that support Wi-Fi Access Point (AP) mode. Future versions may support other connection methods.

docs.title: How to get a microcontroller
docs.text:
These boards are widely available, so you shouldn't have any trouble finding one. You can order them from a specialized electronics retailer, buy them on the usual online marketplaces, or even pick one up at a physical store — whichever suits you best.

Here are a few sources worth checking out:

  • Amazon
  • Conrad
  • Mouser
  • Aliexpress

docs.title: Once you receive your microcontroller
docs.text:
Head over to horcrux flash, select your board, and download the matching firmware. To make sure you get the latest version of horcrux-core, click on Latest GitHub Release.

Once the firmware is downloaded, you'll see a Qrcode that you can then scan with your phone to join the network.

More information about the flash process can be found here.
